NKE.rationale: Nike is in severe fundamental deterioration across all key metrics. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with net margin operating margins collapsing % YoY. Operating cash flow collapsed 76% YoY. Revenue was essentially flat YoY (+0.1% YoY) but operating income plunged 23% to $650M. The trajectory is alarming: Q2→Q3 saw EPS drop from $0. to to000 operating margin compression from from from.. from .% to 6.2% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% to 4.8% and 4.8% and 4.8% to 4.8% and 4.8% and 4.8% and 4.8% and 4.8% (from 12.8% in 2021), and operating margin at 6.2% is dangerously thin. ROE has collapsed from 32.2% to 16% over the past year. The company faces structural headwinds: global athletic footwear market share fell to 22.9% (down 3pp YoY per Euromonitor), 37% of assortment sold at discounts, and China sales declining 10% with local brand competition intensifying. Two rounds of layoffs affecting 14,000 employees signal deep operational restructuring. The EEOC investigation into DEI practices adds regulatory and reputational risk. Valuation at 29x PE is expensive for a business with collapsing margins and negative earnings trajectory—the PE was 19x a year ago when earnings were stronger, meaning the market is now paying more for less. Short interest has risen to 4.67% from 0.41% at CEO Hill's appointment. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.317 over 90 days, with consistent -1.0 readings in April-May 2026). The stock is down 29% in the last quarter and 76% from its 2021 peak. No credible near-term catalyst exists—management guided for continued low single-digit revenue declines over the next three quarters and delayed gross margin expansion to Q2 2027. The dividend of $0.41/quarter (3.7% yield) is not well covered by earnings or free cash flow, creating further risk. All three pillars—deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation vs. history, and absence of positive near-term catalysts—point decisively negative.
